examples.solution_text:
Differentiate:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=2x-8\end{aligned}$

(a) A horizontal tangent has gradient $0$.
$\begin{aligned}2x-8&=0\\2x&=8\\x&=4\\f(4)&=4^2-8(4)+13\\&=-3\end{aligned}$
The point is $(4,-3)$.

(b) Set the derivative equal to $4$.
$\begin{aligned}2x-8&=4\\2x&=12\\x&=6\\f(6)&=6^2-8(6)+13\\&=1\end{aligned}$
The point is $(6,1)$. Each ordinate comes from $f(x)$, not $f'(x)$.

examples.question_text: Find all points on $y=\dfrac{x^3}{3}-2x+4$ where the tangent has gradient $7$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=x^2-2\\x^2-2&=7\\x^2&=9\\x&=\pm3\end{aligned}$

Substitute both values into the curve.
$\begin{aligned}f(3)&=\frac{3^3}{3}-2(3)+4\\&=7\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f(-3)&=\frac{(-3)^3}{3}-2(-3)+4\\&=1\end{aligned}$
The points are $(3,7)$ and $(-3,1)$.

At a stationary point, the tangent is horizontal.
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=4x^3-16x\\4x^3-16x&=0\\4x(x-2)(x+2)&=0\end{aligned}$
Thus $x=0$, $x=2$ or $x=-2$.

$\begin{aligned}f(0)&=6\\f(2)&=2^4-8(2)^2+6\\&=-10\\f(-2)&=(-2)^4-8(-2)^2+6\\&=-10\end{aligned}$
The stationary points are $(0,6)$, $(2,-10)$ and $(-2,-10)$.

examples.question_text: Find the point on $y=x^2-7x+3$ where the normal has gradient $\dfrac13$.
examples.solution_text:
The tangent and normal are perpendicular.
$\begin{aligned}m_t&=-\frac{1}{m_n}\\&=-\frac{1}{1/3}\\&=-3\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=2x-7\\2x-7&=-3\\2x&=4\\x&=2\\f(2)&=2^2-7(2)+3\\&=-7\end{aligned}$
The point is $(2,-7)$.

examples.question_text: Find the point on $y=2x^2-5x+4$ where the tangent is parallel to $3x-y+2=0$.
Find the point on $y=x^2-4x+6$ where the tangent is perpendicular to $2x-y+5=0$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}2x-y+5&=0\\y&=2x+5\end{aligned}$
The given line has gradient $2$, so the perpendicular tangent has gradient $-\dfrac12$.

$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=2x-4\\2x-4&=-\frac12\\2x&=\frac72\\x&=\frac74\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f\left(\frac74\right)&=\left(\frac74\right)^2-4\left(\frac74\right)+6\\&=\frac{49}{16}-7+6\\&=\frac{33}{16}\end{aligned}$
The point is $\left(\dfrac74,\dfrac{33}{16}\right)$.

examples.question_text: Find the point on $y=x^3-3x^2+5$ with $x>1$ where the tangent is parallel to $9x-y-2=0$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}9x-y-2&=0\\y&=9x-2\end{aligned}$
The required tangent gradient is $9$.

$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=3x^2-6x\\3x^2-6x&=9\\3x^2-6x-9&=0\\3(x-3)(x+1)&=0\end{aligned}$
The candidate values are $x=3$ and $x=-1$. Only $x=3$ satisfies $x>1$.

$\begin{aligned}f(3)&=3^3-3(3)^2+5\\&=5\end{aligned}$
The point is $(3,5)$.

examples.derivation: f'(x)=2x-8. Gradient 0 gives x=4 and f(4)=-3; gradient 4 gives x=6 and f(6)=1.
f'(x)=x²-2. Setting this equal to 7 gives x=±3. Substitution gives f(3)=7 and f(-3)=1.
f'(x)=4x³-16x=4x(x-2)(x+2). Its zeros are 0 and ±2; the corresponding ordinates are 6, -10 and -10.
Normal gradient 1/3 gives tangent gradient -3. Solving 2x-7=-3 gives x=2; f(2)=4-14+3=-7.

The given line is y=3x+2. Solving f'(x)=4x-5=3 gives x=2 and f(2)=2. The illustrated tangent y=3x-4 passes through (2,2), has gradient 3 and matches the curve's derivative there. Both plotted lines and their labels agree with their equations.
The given line has gradient 2, so the perpendicular tangent gradient is -1/2. Solving 2x-4=-1/2 gives x=7/4. Substitution gives 49/16-7+6=33/16.
The given line has gradient 9. Solving 3x²-6x=9 gives 3(x-3)(x+1)=0. Only x=3 satisfies x>1; f(3)=27-27+5=5.
